one_paragraph_summary: Please indulge this ancient grandfather as he revels in the simultaneous but separate grants of master's degree scholarships by top schools in the United States to his three grandchildren.' Panganiban profiles each. Andrea P. Manalac -- natural artist since age three, lead-singer roles from age five in Hoboken, New Jersey, 'Hamilton' five times in three countries but 'Ageless Passion' her favorite (Hahaha!), 36 of 47 Walt Disney World attractions in one day, Disney Parks in Hong Kong, Tokyo, Paris, LA, and Orlando across 2011-2012, and a career arc from Shopee recruiter to HR business partner to PwC senior consultant -- eagerly chose the University of Michigan MBA, her mother's alma mater. Rafa P. Yaptangco -- quiet but not shy, lead dancer at Ridgefield Kindergarten and Southridge, Ateneo graduate of June 2019 ('Dad and Mom, I passed my Filipino final exams!'), held a golf club at age three with a single-digit handicap by 2024 (after a 30→10 COVID-era jump and a recent round at Pebble Beach), and tonsillitis-era screen time that turned into a tech-support 'competitive advantage' -- went from Lazada user-growth analyst to TikTok e-commerce growth marketing manager and now Fordham University MBA with a 'formidable dean's scholarship' (to the delight of Fr. Bobby Yap). Victoria P. Hannett -- Greenwich, Connecticut native; avid dancer from age two to seventeen; top 0.1% Taylor Swift fan on Spotify; math whiz skipping sixth-grade math; Georgetown Neurobiology graduate two weeks before the column -- pursues a Master of Biotechnology at the University of Pennsylvania, focused on drug discovery for migraine (her mother's affliction), stroke (cause of death of both paternal grandparents), dementia, and ADHD; she applied to seven top US universities, was accepted by all, and was offered scholarships in five -- 'champagne problems,' to borrow Taylor Swift's phrase. 'Mabuhay! Amazing indeed, all my three apo applied merely for admissions but were offered multiple scholarships. My Leni joins me from heaven in thanking our Lord for His grant of these incalculable blessings to my family.'
